[page[title]]

IHostExtensions must route requested command details to a handling service resolved from the service provider.

What the Standard says

“route” — Configuration models may route incoming operations to their respective functions. IHostExtensions performs that configuration responsibility for a requested command. read it here.
“routing” — Exposure models route each request or call to the appropriate operational model. Resolving the command handler from the service provider preserves that thin exposure behavior. read it here.

Why it matters

The root extension should route command details to a handler resolved by the service provider. This preserves inversion of control and keeps command selection at the exposure boundary while the handling service owns the actual operation.

Bad code example

if (args[0] == "import")
{
    // Command implementation lives in the root exposure.
}

Good code example

ICommandHandlingService handler =
    host.Services.GetRequiredKeyedService<ICommandHandlingService>(args[0]);

return handler.HandleAsync(args);
